questions.question: Where must zero rows appear in row echelon form?
options: At the bottom of the matrix.
Anywhere, as they hold no pivots.
Only between nonzero rows.
At the top of the matrix.

questions.question: How must pivots move as one goes down the rows in row echelon form?
options: Each pivot must lie exactly one column right of the one above.
Each pivot must lie to the left of the pivot above it.
Each pivot must lie in the same column as the pivot above.
Each pivot must lie to the right of the pivot above it.

questions.question: Which matrix is in row echelon form?
options: $\begin{pmatrix}0&0&1\\1&0&0\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}2&1&-2\\0&3&-4\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}1&2&-1\\0&3&-2\\0&1&4\end{pmatrix}$

questions.question: Why is $\begin{pmatrix}0&0&1\\1&0&0\end{pmatrix}$ not in row echelon form?
options: The first row starts with zeros, which echelon form forbids.
Column $2$ has no pivot, but every column needs one.
A $2\times3$ matrix needs a zero row to be in echelon form.
The second row's pivot lies left of the pivot above it.

questions.question: Can a matrix in row echelon form have a pivot that is not equal to $1$?
options: Yes, echelon form does not require pivots equal to $1$.
Yes, but only if each pivot is positive, like $2$ or $3$.
No, every pivot must be scaled to $1$ in echelon form.
No, a pivot is by definition the first entry equal to $1$.

questions.question: What is the rank of $\begin{pmatrix}1&2&0\\0&0&5\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}$ if it is in row echelon form?
Which augmented matrix in row echelon form represents a contradiction?
options: $\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}0&1&2\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}$

questions.question: Which common reduced form characterises two row-equivalent matrices?
options: any row echelon form (REF) of the matrix
the rank together with the matrix size
reduced row echelon form (RREF)
the determinant of the matrix

questions.question: A matrix $\boldsymbol{A}$ is brought to row echelon form in two different ways, and the two resulting matrices differ. Which feature must they share?
options: The columns that contain the pivots.
The values of the pivots.
The entries above each pivot.
Nothing, since row echelon form is not unique.

questions.question: Which matrix is in row echelon form but not in reduced row echelon form?
options: $\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$
